solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One keen on shooting spy's device on screen

parts.note: a shutter is a panel that screens a window
a bug is a hidden listening device used in spying

explanation.surface: A sniper or agent peering through a camera hidden behind a screen.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' puts the spy's device after the screen. 'Shooting' suggests guns, but here it means taking photographs.
explanation.definitionFit: A shutterbug is an informal name for an enthusiastic amateur photographer, someone who loves taking pictures.

clue.text: Vocal greeting stresses what looks like a guinea pig

definitions.text: what looks like a guinea pig

indicators.note: something vocal is spoken, so we want the sound of the words rather than their spelling

parts.note: hi is a greeting and racks means stresses or strains

explanation.surface: Someone's loud hello puts strain on a small guinea-pig-like creature.
explanation.walkthrough: Said together, 'hi' and 'racks' make the animal's name: HYRAX.
explanation.definitionFit: The hyrax is a small furry African mammal, rounded and short-eared, often compared in looks to a large guinea pig or rodent.

clue.text: Raises rents declared in the higher flats?

parts.note: to up something is to raise it

indicators.note: to declare is to say out loud, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: rents are tears or rips, and tears in that sense rhymes with stairs

explanation.surface: A landlord announces rent rises for the flats on the upper floors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rents' looks like money paid to a landlord, but it is the noun meaning rips. The question mark flags a definition by example: living upstairs.
explanation.definitionFit: In a block, the higher flats are reached by climbing, so being in one means being on an upper floor of the building.

clue.text: Ghanaian garment's not right

indicators.note: saying something is not there tells us to remove it from the word

parts.note: a T-shirt is a common garment
RT is a standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A piece of Ghanaian clothing is described as not quite right.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the two-letter abbreviation RT, not just R, from the end of T-SHIRT. 'Ghanaian garment' reads as one phrase, but only the first word is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tshi, also spelt Twi, names a people of Ghana and their language, so it serves as a word for Ghanaian.

clue.text: Hook ingoing in play following Tinkerbell's lead

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the piece named first is placed second
the lead of something is its front, so only the opening letter is wanted

parts.note: the initial of the fairy's name
Enter is the stage direction in a script for a character coming on

explanation.surface: Captain Hook makes his entrance in Peter Pan, just after Tinkerbell.
explanation.walkthrough: Hook and Tinkerbell paint Peter Pan, but Hook is the plain definition. 'Following' places the stage direction after the initial.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenter is one of the hooks on a frame used to stretch cloth, the source of the phrase on tenterhooks.

clue.text: Venomous fish scares as swimming

indicators.note: letters that are swimming move freely about, so they can settle in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A poisonous fish frightens people while it is swimming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swimming' belongs to the fish picture, which is why it hides well as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The rascasse is a scorpionfish of the Mediterranean, used in bouillabaisse, whose spines carry venom.

clue.text: Some felt the French missed out in conflict

indicators.note: something missed out is omitted, so those letters are taken away

parts.note: a battle is an armed conflict
le is the French masculine word for the

explanation.surface: Some people felt the French were left out of a war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Felt' reads as the past tense of feel, but it is the fabric. 'In conflict' supplies the word to cut from.
explanation.definitionFit: Batt is a sheet of matted fibre or wadding, and a felted piece of such material counts as a batt.

clue.text: Doomed flier going up with tail gone left base for life

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading from bottom to top
a tail is the final part, and losing it drops the last letter

parts.note: Icarus flew too near the sun on wax wings and fell to his death
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A doomed pilot climbs, loses his tail and leaves his base for good.
explanation.walkthrough: Myth's doomed flier fell and never went up, which is the joke. 'Base' reads as an airbase, but it is a chemical base.
explanation.definitionFit: Uracil is one of the four nucleobases in RNA, so it is a chemical base essential to living things.

clue.text: What enameller inlays worked all round pin

indicators.note: worked material has been reshaped, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
O is round in shape
taken as written

explanation.surface: A craftsman works enamel all round a brooch pin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All round' reads as a phrase meaning around, but it splits into two pieces of fodder. The shuffled letters follow 'worked'.
explanation.definitionFit: A paillon is a small piece of metal foil laid into enamel work for brilliance, so it is something an enameller sets in.

clue.text: With a square of columns seen neatly arranged

indicators.note: arranging letters puts them into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An architect admires a square of columns laid out neatly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A square of columns' sounds like a colonnaded courtyard, but it is arithmetic: three squared is nine.
explanation.definitionFit: Enneastyle describes a classical portico having nine columns, and nine is the square of three.

clue.text: Daisy's part in male spy coming back

indicators.note: coming back means travelling the other way, so the run is read right to left
the letters sit inside the following words, spanning their boundaries

parts.note: the run of letters across the end of 'male', all of 'spy' and the start of 'coming'

explanation.surface: Someone plays the role of Daisy in a spy drama about a returning agent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daisy' looks like a character in a spy story, but it is the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A cypsela is the dry one-seeded fruit of daisies and other composite plants, a botanical part of the flower.

clue.text: Timber tree area queen once opened

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for area
R stands for Regina, Latin for queen
gan is an old word for began, and 'once' flags the archaism

explanation.surface: A queen once opened an area planted with timber trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opened' reads as a ceremony, but here it means started, in the archaic form 'gan'.
explanation.definitionFit: The argan is a thorny Moroccan tree valued for its hard wood and for the oil pressed from its kernels.

clue.text: Use up earlier price green menus being revised

parts.note: pr. is a recognised abbreviation for price

indicators.note: a revised version has been reworked, so its letters come out in another order

parts.note: eco is a prefix meaning environmentally friendly, or green
taken as written

explanation.surface: A restaurant spends its budget early because its prices and vegetarian menus are being rewritten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Price green' reads as one phrase, but it splits into an abbreviation and a short word for environmentally friendly.
explanation.definitionFit: To preconsume is to consume beforehand, and consuming something means using it up, so this is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Candida's killer hiding over in Grand Central?

indicators.note: something hiding is no longer visible, so it leaves the word

parts.note: Grand Central is a railway station in New York, abbreviated NY
O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A killer hides out in New York's Grand Central, with Candida as the victim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Candida' reads as a woman's name, but it is a fungus. The question mark admits that Grand Central is an example of a New York station.
explanation.definitionFit: Nystatin is an antifungal drug used to treat thrush, which is caused by the yeast Candida, so it kills it.

clue.text: Thor's reed boat sounded dangerous without a keel

parts.note: Ra was the papyrus reed boat Thor Heyerdahl sailed across the Atlantic

indicators.note: something sounded is spoken out, so the word is taken by its pronunciation

parts.note: a tight spot is a dangerous one

explanation.surface: The explorer's reed boat seemed perilous because it had no keel.
explanation.walkthrough: Thor is the explorer Thor Heyerdahl, not the Norse god. 'Without a keel' reads as a boat's flaw but describes a bird's breastbone.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratite birds such as ostriches lack the keeled breastbone that anchors flight muscles, so ratite means having an unkeeled sternum.

clue.text: Pass the last of the cabbage

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass

indicators.note: the last of something is its final part, so only the end letter is taken

parts.note: the final letter of the second small word

explanation.surface: At dinner, someone asks for the rest of the cabbage to be handed over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass' sounds like handing a dish along, but it is a gap between mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: Cole is an old general name for plants of the cabbage family, surviving in coleslaw and colewort.

clue.text: Test executed in the morning

parts.note: to ex is to cross out or do away with, so something executed has been exed
a.m. marks times in the morning

explanation.surface: A test was carried out first thing in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Executed' reads as carried out, but it is taken in the sense of killed off or crossed out.
explanation.definitionFit: An exam is a formal examination of knowledge, and test is its everyday synonym.

clue.text: Rail about suitable plant producing detergent

indicators.note: about means around, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: the soree, or sora, is a small American bird of the rail family
apt means suitable

explanation.surface: Someone protests about a suitable factory making washing powder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rail' reads as a verb meaning complain, and 'plant' as a factory; one is a bird and the other a growing thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Soap trees are trees whose bark or fruit contains saponins, which lather in water and were used for washing.

clue.text: Armpit cut badly by one in Texas

parts.note: AX is the American spelling of axe, to cut
ill means badly, as in ill-treated
a means one
gives no letters; it asks for the cut word in its American spelling

explanation.surface: Someone in Texas has a badly gashed armpit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In Texas' attaches to 'cut', asking for the American spelling. 'By' is part of the scene but works to join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Axilla is the anatomical Latin term for the armpit, the hollow under the junction of arm and shoulder.

clue.text: Adores Scots part of earth's crust of loamy deposits

parts.note: loe is a Scots form of love
sial is the upper layer of the earth's crust, rich in silica and alumina

explanation.surface: Scots are fond of the rich soil in their part of the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scots' reads as the people doing the adoring, but it marks the Scots dialect word.
explanation.definitionFit: Loess is fine windblown loam or silt, and loessial is its adjective, describing things made of such deposits.

clue.text: Wicker basket appeared full of holes

parts.note: a crib can be a wicker basket or manger
rose means came up, as the sun appears

explanation.surface: A wicker basket looked as though it were riddled with holes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appeared full of holes' reads as one phrase, but the verb is wordplay and the definition starts after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Cribrose is a rare botanical word meaning perforated like a sieve, from Latin cribrum, a sieve.

clue.text: Row over Julia removing Japanese plant

indicators.note: turning something over flips it, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: an oar is used to row a boat

indicators.note: removing means taking away, so one letter drops out

parts.note: taken as written
J is the abbreviation for Japanese

explanation.surface: An argument over Julia ends with a Japanese plant being taken away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' reads as a quarrel, but it is the rowing kind. 'Japanese plant' reads as one thing, but the plant comes from New Zealand.
explanation.definitionFit: Raoulia is a genus of cushion-forming New Zealand plants, some called vegetable sheep because they look like resting sheep.

clue.text: Child with hostility for climbing cat

parts.note: ch. is the abbreviation for child

indicators.note: climbing in a down entry means going upwards, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: hate is strong hostility

explanation.surface: A child, hostile to cats, climbs a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climbing cat' sounds like a tree-climbing animal, but 'climbing' belongs to the wordplay. This is a variant spelling of a familiar big cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Chetah is an older spelling of cheetah, the spotted big cat famed for its speed.

clue.text: Give decoration to idiot people in part

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece is surrounded

parts.note: pt is the abbreviation for part
an ass is a fool
men are people

explanation.surface: A fool is given a medal for playing a part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give decoration to' sounds like awarding a medal, but it is a verb for trimming cloth. 'Part' supplies the outside letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Passment, or passement, is decorative braid or lace edging, and as a verb it means to trim with such ornament.

clue.text: March locally in South Dakota went smoothly in the past

indicators.note: being in a place means being enclosed by it

parts.note: SD is the postal abbreviation for South Dakota
Lide is a dialect name for the month of March

explanation.surface: A march held locally in South Dakota went off without a hitch years ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'March' reads as a protest walk, but it is the month, in a regional word. 'In the past' marks an old verb form.
explanation.definitionFit: Slided is an archaic past tense of slide, and sliding is moving smoothly over a surface.

clue.text: Numbers rise going without hot substantial meal

indicators.note: without can mean outside, so this piece goes around the other

parts.note: nos. is the abbreviation for numbers
H for hot, as on a tap
up is a rise, as in ups and downs

explanation.surface: Numbers go up as people do without a hot dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' reads as lacking, but in crosswords it can mean outside. 'Nosh' is British slang for food.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosh-up is informal British slang for a large, filling meal or feast.

clue.text: Cool box weather after the end of June

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, the only one kept

parts.note: its final letter
the sky stands for the weather, as in grey skies

explanation.surface: Once June is over, the weather calls for a cool box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' places the weather word behind the single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Esky is an Australian brand name for a portable insulated cool box, used there as the generic word.

clue.text: Silk fabric formerly known to English

parts.note: kent is an old and Scots past participle of ken, to know
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A silk fabric used to be familiar to the English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Formerly' signals an archaic verb form, not a past time in the surface story.
explanation.definitionFit: Kente is a brightly woven Ghanaian cloth, traditionally made in strips of silk or cotton.

clue.text: Make legal claim about quiet actor staying silent

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps round another

parts.note: to sue is to bring a legal claim
p for piano, quiet in music

explanation.surface: Someone sues over a quiet actor who refuses to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quiet' and 'silent' look like one idea repeated, but the first is wordplay and the second part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A supe, short for supernumerary, is an extra on stage who appears without any lines.

clue.text: Reported wages — note foreign currency

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so its sound counts

parts.note: pay is a word for wages
so, or soh, is the fifth note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A news report on pay notes that it is in a foreign currency.
explanation.walkthrough: The first syllable is the sound of the wages word, written as the currency spells it.
explanation.definitionFit: The peso is the monetary unit of Mexico, Argentina and several other countries, so a foreign currency to Britons.

clue.text: Light biscuits mostly used to line dessert

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: kisses are small light meringue biscuits
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: Light biscuits are used to line a pudding dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Line' reads as a verb about lining a dish, but it gives one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Kissel is a Russian dessert of fruit juice thickened with starch, served as a sweet jelly or soup.

clue.text: Navy where it should be army

indicators.note: naming the proper place of something puts it inside that place

parts.note: a navy's proper place is the sea
N is the abbreviation for navy

explanation.surface: A complaint that the navy has turned up where the army ought to be.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase both places the letter and supplies the sea around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sena is the Hindi and Urdu word for an army, familiar from Indian names such as the Bharatiya Sena.

clue.text: Wearing a thick coat resulted in chaos

indicators.note: things in chaos are thrown into disorder, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Putting on a heavy coat led to disorder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resulted in chaos' reads as a single verb phrase, but 'in chaos' is the instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: An ulster is a long, loose, heavy overcoat, originally made in Ulster, so being ulstered is being dressed in one.

clue.text: Monkey I had kept in house in Provence

indicators.note: what is kept in a place is held within it

parts.note: a mas is a traditional farmhouse in Provence
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: Someone kept a pet monkey in their farmhouse in Provence.
explanation.walkthrough: The French farmhouse word goes round the contraction.
explanation.definitionFit: Midas is a former genus name for tamarins, small South American monkeys, still found in Chambers as a monkey.

clue.text: As dictated by the case before National Academy

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
Nat. is the abbreviation for National
A is the abbreviation for Academy

explanation.surface: Proceedings at a national academy follow whatever the case requires.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' sounds legal, but the definition is a Latin phrase, so the enumeration 1,2,4 splits it oddly from the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: E re nata is a Latin phrase meaning according to the circumstances, from the matter that has arisen.

clue.text: Order for poppies? Here's a load sent out

indicators.note: things sent out are scattered, so the letters disperse into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A customer orders flowers, and a whole delivery of poppies goes out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' sounds like a purchase, but it is the biological rank. The question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhoeadales is an older name for the plant order containing the poppy family, Papaveraceae, a taxonomic classification.
